parts.problem_md:
The population of a city is $4.2\times10^{6}$.

It increases by 5% in one year.

Write the new population in standard form.
parts.solution_md:
> *Use a multiplier of 1.05 to increase by 5% (use your calculator for this)*

$( 4.2 \times 10^{6} ) \times 1.05 = 4 410 000$

**[M1]**

> *Write this in standard form, *$a\times10^{n}$* where *$a$* is between 1 and 10*

$4.41\times10^{6}$

**[A1]**

parts.problem_md:
The table shows some information about eight planets.

| **Planet** | **Distance from Earth (km)** | **Mass (kg)** |
|---|---|---|
| Earth | 0 | 5.97 $\times$10<sup>24</sup> |
| Jupiter | 6.29 $\times$ 10<sup>8</sup> | 1.898 $\times$ 10<sup>27</sup> |
| Mars | 7.83 $\times$ 10<sup>7</sup> | 6.42 $\times$ 10<sup>23</sup> |
| Mercury | 9.17 $\times$ 10<sup>7</sup> | 3.302 $\times$ 10<sup>23</sup> |
| Neptune | 4.35 $\times$ 10<sup>9</sup> | 1.024 $\times$ 10<sup>26</sup> |
| Saturn | 1.28 $\times$ 10<sup>9</sup> | 5.68 $\times$ 10<sup>26</sup> |
| Uranus | 2.72  $\times$ 10<sup>9</sup> | 8.683 $\times$ 10<sup>25</sup> |
| Venus | 4.14  $\times$ 10<sup>7</sup> | 4.869 $\times$ 10<sup>24</sup> |

Write down the name of the planet with the greatest mass.
parts.solution_md:
> *All of the masses are given in standard form, **a **× 10*<sup>*n*</sup><sup>* *</sup>*, where 1 ≤ **a **< 10, so the planet with the greatest mass is the planet with the greatest value of **n.** *

**Jupiter**** [1]**

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

| Mercury | 9.17 ![cross times] 10^7^ | 3.302 ![cross times] 10^23^ |
| Venus | 4.14  ![cross times] 10^7^ | 4.869 ![cross times] 10^24^ |

Find the difference between the mass of Venus and the mass of Mercury.
parts.solution_md:
> *Identify the calculation.*

*Mass (Venus) - mass (Mercury) = 4.869 × 10**<sup>24</sup>** - 3.302 × 10**<sup>23</sup>*

> *Type the problem directly into your calculator.*

*4.869 × 10**<sup>24</sup>** - 3.302 × 10**<sup>23</sup>** = 4.5388 × 10**<sup>24</sup>*

**4.5388 × 10**<sup>**24**</sup>** kg ****[1]**

| Neptune | 4.35 ![cross times] 10^9^ |
| Venus | 4.14  ![cross times] 10^7^ |

Nishat says that Neptune is over a hundred times further away from Earth than Venus is.

Is Nishat right? 
You must show how you get your answer.
parts.solution_md:

$\frac{\mathrm{Distance}(\mathrm{Neptune})}{\mathrm{Distance}(\mathrm{Venus})}=\frac{4.35\times10^{9}}{4.14\times10^{7}}$

> *Type the problem directly into your calculator.*

$\frac{4.35\times10^{9}}{4.14\times10^{7}}=105.072...$

**[1] **
**Yes, because 105.07... > 100  ****[1]**

parts.problem_md:
$T=\sqrt{\frac{w}{d^{3}}}\,w=5.6\times10^{-5}\,d=1.4\times10^{-4}$

Work out the value of *T*. 
Give your answer in standard form correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.solution_md:
> *Substitute the values given for **w **and **d **into the expression for **T**.*

$T = \sqrt{ \frac{ 5.6 \times 10^{- 5} }{( 1.4 \times 10^{- 4} )^{3}} }$

> *Type the problem into your calculator, use the square root, fraction, standard form buttons and the arrow keys to type the whole expression in in one go.*

$\sqrt{ \frac{ 5.6 \times 10^{- 5} }{( 1.4 \times 10^{- 4} )^{3}} } = 4517.5395...$

** ****[1]**

> *Convert to standard form.*

$\begin{gathered} 4517.5395... & = 4.517539... \times 1000 \\ = 4.517539... \times 10^{3} \end{gathered}$

** ****[1]**

> *Round your answer to 3 significant figures. The third significant figure is the digit 1, however this is followed by a 7 which is greater than 5 s round it up to a 2.*

**4.52 × 10**<sup>**3**</sup>** ****[1]**

equations.alt:

w = 5.6 x 10 ^ - 5
d = 1.4 x 10 ^ - 4

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

T = sqrt(w / d^3)

*w* is increased by 10% *d* is increased by 5%

Lottie says,

"The value of *T* will increase because both *w* and *d* are increased."

Lottie is wrong. 
Explain why.
parts.solution_md:
> *To increase **w** by 10%, multiply it by 1.1 and to increase **d** by 5% multiply it by 1.05.*

> *Therefore **T **will become:*

> $T = \sqrt{ \frac{w \times 1.1}{( d \times 1.05 )^{3}} } = \sqrt{ \frac{5.6 \times 10^{- 5} \times 1.1}{( 1.4 \times 10^{- 4} \times 1.05 )^{3}} } = 4403.66....$* *

**[1]**

> *The increase of 5% on the denominator is cubed, whilst the increase on the numerator is not, therefore the scale factor is less than 1 so **T **decreases.*

**4.40... × 10**<sup>**3**</sup>**  <  4.51... × 10**<sup>**3**</sup>
<sup>** **</sup>**T ****has decreased ****[1]**

$\sqrt{ \frac{ 8.5 \times 10^{9 - 4 \times 10^{8} }{( 8.5 \times 10^{9} ) ( 4 \times 10^{8} )} } = 4.880935... \times 10^{-5} }$

* Either part of the fraction evaluated correctly **[1] ** *

**4.9 × 10**<sup>**-5**</sup>** ****[1]**

parts.problem_md: Find the exact value of $8^{\frac{2}{3}}\times49^{-\frac{1}{2}}$.
parts.solution_md:
> *The key here is the word "exact". *
*This means you can't just work it out on your calculator and give the answer "0.5714...", as you'd have to round it- so it's not exact! *
*Instead you need to apply laws of fractional and negative indices*
* *`x ^ a / b = ( b-th sqrt of x ) ^ a`* so  *

$8^{ \frac{2}{3} } = ( \sqrt[3]{8} )^{2} = 2^{2} = 4$

> $x^{-c}=\frac{1}{x^{c}}$* so*

$\begin{array}{rcl} 49^{- 1 \frac{1}{2}} & = \frac{1}{ \sqrt{49} } = \frac{1}{7} \end{array}$

*either** 4 **or *$\frac{1}{7}$** ****[1]**

> *Finally multiply the two results together*

* *$\begin{gathered} 4 \times \frac{1}{7} & = \frac{4}{7} \end{gathered}$

$\frac{4}{7}$** [1]**
